correctness.rationale: In weighted projective P(1,1,1,3), off the singular point (u,v)!=0 forces scaling=1 for an involution-fixed point, so w=y=0 and six simple roots of the source smooth binary sextic c6 are the complete smooth locus. At w=1 over p=[0:0:1], weight-three rescaling gives local (u,v,y)->(-u,-v,y). Equivariant A_(2n+1) plane-branch normal form x²+z^(2n+2) yields surface UV=z^N with N=2n+2 and involution (U,V,z)->(V,U,-z). The minimal A_(N-1) exceptional chain reverses j to N-j. The sole preserved E_(N/2) has toric coordinate q=(s/t)^(N/2) transformed to (-1)^(N/2)/q, yielding exactly two simple fixed q roots over C; neighboring nodes exchanged, no extra fixed points. Generic smoothness and singularity hypotheses follow the inspected source Theorem 2.1/Proposition 2.3, not a finite experiment. The elementary bundled n=1..8 script checks only polynomial consequences and is not mistaken for resolution proof.

value.rationale: An exact localization of a natural symplectic involution on canonical projective K3 models has geometric value beyond its known total cardinality: it identifies which resolved singular component carries the remaining two points and which smooth branch points are fixed, making quotient geometry and local actions transparent. The family is a motivated published model, not an arbitrary finite example.

final_claim: For a general complex L-polarized K3 in the specified canonical irreducible biquadratic double-sextic family with rho_L>10, excluding H+D8+D4, the symplectic involution (w,y)->(-w,-y) has exactly six smooth fixed Weierstrass points w=y=0,c6(u,v)=0 and exactly two additional fixed points on the central exceptional component E_(n+1) of the A_(2n+1) resolution, n=rho_L-10.
limitations: Complex, general irreducible-sextic cases only with rho_L>10; H+D8+D4 and H+N constructions excluded.
No explicit quotient surface classification claimed; generic fixed-point total is classical.
